details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:241-279 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Both changelog sync steps run `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` from the fetched `@stable` checkout, so the consumer repo is executing upstream code that writes into its filesystem.
  WHY: This is the intended design per the reviewer, so it does not create a new trust boundary, but it is still execution of fetched code.
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:148-230 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Blank-line insertion logic in `_ensure_unreleased_section` / `_plan_keep_a_changelog` can produce double blank lines or incorrect spacing when inserting new subsections or creating Unreleased from scratch.
  WHY: That breaks the additive formatting contract and can create spurious diffs or non-idempotent formatting.
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:318 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: Tail insertion for a new subsection adds a leading blank line even when the existing content already ends with one.
  WHY: Repeated assembly can accumulate double-blank-line diffs.
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:340-344 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: Appending to an existing same-day date heading prepends another blank line on top of the existing trailing blank line.
  WHY: Repeated assembly can accumulate extra blank lines in the date-heading layout.
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:429-634 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `changed_paths` hardcodes `FRAGMENTS_DIRNAME` / `"changelog.d"` instead of deriving the resolved `fragments_dir`, so `--changed-paths-file` can report the wrong directory for non-default fragment locations.
  WHY: Severity disagreement: moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 rated it MAJOR/high while the others rated it NIT/low; the highest severity is high, and the path list will be wrong whenever `--fragments-dir` is overridden.
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml:460-523 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The release assembly step writes `changelog_assembled`, `changelog_fragment_count`, and `changelog_layout` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, but the workflow never exposes those as declared step outputs.
  WHY: The consumer sync path reads those outputs from its own step, so the release-job contract is inconsistent and future reuse would see empty values.
- agents.md:626-643 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The rewritten changelog paragraph still points at `docs/changelog-style.md` as if it were consumer-visible.
  WHY: The reviewer says consumer repos do not receive that file, so the reference remains a dangling pointer in the consumer context.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: PR description acceptance criteria states the fragment should follow `changelog.d/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md` naming and §20's entry structure (headline, lead paragraph, numbers, audience closing, optional contributor section).
  expected_change_site: changelog.d/changelog-fragment-workflow.md
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The fragment exists and is structurally complete, but the slug `changelog-fragment-workflow.md` uses a generic "workflow" term rather than a descriptive kebab-case slug that reflects the actual change; the entry body also blends the headline and lead paragraph into one dense paragraph instead of the §20 template's clearer separation.
- requirement: "Dogfoods the rule: its own entry is changelog.d/changelog-fragment-workflow.md, not a CHANGELOG.md edit."
  expected_change_site: changelog.d/changelog-fragment-workflow.md
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  EVIDENCE: The file exists in the PR diff and CHANGELOG.md is not touched, but the content is self-referential, includes operational tables and implementation details, and does not fully follow the voice guidance in CLAUDE.md §20.
- requirement: “The new script is wired into existing automation and registered in docs/scripts-pending-removal.md with all six required fields.”
  expected_change_site: docs/scripts-pending-removal.md (registry entry) + .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml and .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: The registry entry exists and is complete, but the release workflows do not emit the `changelog_assembled` / `changelog_layout` outputs that the consumer sync path depends on and that the script itself writes to GITHUB_OUTPUT.
- requirement: “§20 is self-contained — no reference to a file absent from consumer repos, and it states explicitly when an entry is required.”
  expected_change_site: CLAUDE.md §20 (and the agents.md summary of it)
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  EVIDENCE: `agents.md:635` still says `docs/changelog-style.md` is the longer-form contributor-facing companion and lives in this repo only.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:634 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `changed_paths` list hardcodes `FRAGMENTS_DIRNAME` (`"changelog.d"`) rather than computing the actual fragments directory from the `fragments_dir` parameter.
  WHY: If `--fragments-dir` is passed with a non-default value, the `--changed-paths-file` output will list the wrong directory.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml: the new `Sync changelog fragment assets from upstream` step (id: `changelog_sync`) and `Assemble changelog fragments` step (id: `changelog_assemble`) | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Both steps run an upstream Python script (`scripts/assemble_changelog.py`) fetched from the `@stable` support checkout, and that script writes to the consumer repo's filesystem.
  WHY: The reviewer judged this to be intended design and not a new trust boundary, but it is still execution of fetched code.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:318 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When inserting a new subsection at the end of the Unreleased block, the payload starts with `["", f"### {category}", ""]`, which can add a blank line before the new heading even when the existing content already ends with one.
  WHY: This can create double-blank-line diffs and violates additive formatting.
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:340-344 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When appending to an existing same-day date heading, the code adds `[""] + payload_body`, which can double up an already-present trailing blank line.
  WHY: Repeated assembly can accumulate extra blank lines.
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:634 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `changed_paths` is hardcoded as `[str(result["changelog"]), FRAGMENTS_DIRNAME]`, where `FRAGMENTS_DIRNAME = "changelog.d"`.
  WHY: If `--fragments-dir` is passed with a non-default path, `--changed-paths-file` will incorrectly list `changelog.d` instead of the actual path.
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml, .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The release workflow runs the assembler but does not expose `changelog_assembled`, `changelog_layout`, or `changelog_fragment_count` as workflow outputs.
  WHY: The consumer sync path can read outputs from its own step, but the release path leaves the contract inconsistent and the outputs unavailable for future reuse.
- Requirement: "Dogfoods the rule: its own entry is changelog.d/changelog-fragment-workflow.md, not a CHANGELOG.md edit."
  Expected change site: changelog.d/changelog-fragment-workflow.md
  Evidence of absence: The file exists in the PR diff, follows the fragment structure, and CHANGELOG.md is not touched, but the content is self-referential, includes operational tables (`Consumer repos reached: 12`, `Extra GitHub API calls added: 0`), and implementation details (`AUTOFIX_SKIP_SUPPRESS_ON_CONFLICT`), so it doesn't fully follow the voice guidance in CLAUDE.md §20.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:429 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `changed_paths` is set to `[str(result["changelog"]), FRAGMENTS_DIRNAME]`, which hardcodes `"changelog.d"` instead of using the actual `fragments_dir` path that was passed in.
  WHY: If a caller ever passes a non-default `--fragments-dir` argument, the `--changed-paths-file` output will list the wrong directory name.
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml (and identical in test-and-mark-stable.yml):460-523 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The release assembly step runs the assembler which writes `changelog_assembled`, `changelog_fragment_count`, and `changelog_layout` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, but the step never declares those outputs via `outputs:` in the workflow YAML.
  WHY: The consumer sync path reads `steps.changelog_assemble.outputs.changelog_assembled` and `steps.changelog_assemble.outputs.changelog_layout` from its own step, but the release jobs never expose these outputs.
- Requirement: PR description acceptance criteria states the fragment should follow `changelog.d/<issue-or-pr>-<slug>.md` naming and §20's entry structure (headline, lead paragraph, numbers, audience closing, optional contributor section).
  Expected change site: changelog.d/changelog-fragment-workflow.md
  Evidence of absence: The fragment exists and is structurally complete, but the slug `changelog-fragment-workflow.md` uses a generic "workflow" term rather than a descriptive kebab-case slug that reflects the actual change; additionally, the entry body blends the headline and lead paragraph into one dense paragraph rather than following the §20 template's clear separation of headline sentence and 3-5 sentence lead paragraph.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

  PROBLEM: Blank-line insertion logic after new subsections can produce double-blank lines or incorrect spacing when a new subsection is inserted before all existing ones or when the Unreleased block is created from scratch.
  WHY: Inconsistent whitespace violates the purely additive changelog contract and can produce spurious diffs on subsequent assembly runs.
- scripts/assemble_changelog.py:429 | severity=nit | confidence=4
